subject: science

concepts.title: Production of Sound
concepts.definition: Sound is a form of energy generated by the rapid back-and-forth motion or oscillations of an object.
concepts.key_idea: Mechanical vibrations in a source are necessary to create sound waves.
question_patterns: how is sound produced
what causes the sound in a musical instrument
explain the role of vibrations in sound production
why does a vibrating rubber band produce sound

solution_steps.explain: Determine the object that is moving or being struck.
Check if the object is performing periodic to-and-fro motion.

concepts.title: Propagation through a Medium
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the transmission of sound energy from a source to a listener through matter like solids, liquids, or gases.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Sound is a mechanical wave that requires a material medium and cannot travel through a vacuum.
question_patterns: can sound travel in vacuum
why can't astronauts hear each other directly in space
through which medium does sound travel fastest
describe the bell jar experiment

solution_steps.explain: Check if there is matter (air, water, metal) between source and receiver.
If no matter exists, sound propagation is impossible.

concepts.title: Longitudinal Nature of Sound Waves
concepts.definition: In brief, a wave where the medium's individual particles move back and forth in a direction parallel to the wave's path.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Sound propagates as a series of compressions (high density) and rarefactions (low density).
question_patterns: what is a longitudinal wave
define compressions and rarefactions
how do particles move in a sound wave
compare longitudinal and transverse waves

solution_steps.explain: Determine if particles oscillate parallel or perpendicular to the wave.

concepts.title: Frequency and Time Period
concepts.definition: Frequency is the count of complete oscillations per second, while the time period is the duration of one single oscillation.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, both both both both both both both both both both both both Frequency and time period are inversely proportional.
question_patterns: calculate the frequency of a sound wave
find the time period if frequency is ...
how many oscillations occur in one minute
what is the SI unit of frequency

solution_steps.explain: Divide the total number of oscillations by the total time taken.
Take the reciprocal of the frequency.

concepts.title: Wave Speed Relation
concepts.definition: The speed of sound is the product of its wavelength (distance between consecutive crests) and its frequency.
concepts.key_idea: Speed remains constant in a specific medium at a constant temperature, regardless of frequency changes.
question_patterns: calculate the speed of sound
find the wavelength given frequency and speed
what is the frequency if wavelength is ... and speed is ...
how does temperature affect the speed of sound

solution_steps.explain: The product of wavelength and frequency gives the wave speed.

concepts.title: Audible Range
concepts.definition: The specific frequency band that the human ear can detect, typically ranging from 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.
concepts.key_idea: Frequencies below 20 Hz are infrasonic; those above 20 kHz are ultrasonic.
question_patterns: what is the audible range for humans
define infrasonic and ultrasonic waves
can humans hear a frequency of 25 kHz
which animals can hear ultrasound

solution_steps.explain: Compare the given frequency to the 20Hz-20kHz range.

concepts.title: Echo and Reflection
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, the phenomenon where sound is heard again after reflecting off a distant hard surface.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, To hear a distinct echo, the bounced back sound must reach the ear at least 0.1 seconds after the original sound.
question_patterns: calculate the distance to the reflecting wall
what is the minimum distance for an echo
how much time does an echo take to return
why don't we hear echoes in small rooms

solution_steps.explain: Multiply speed by the total time for the sound to go and come back.
The distance to the object is half the total path travelled by the sound.

concepts.title: SONAR (Sound Navigation and Ranging)
concepts.definition: A technology that uses ultrasonic waves to gauge the distance, direction, and speed of underwater objects.
concepts.key_idea: SONAR relies on the principle of echolocation using ultrasound.
question_patterns: how does sonar work
calculate the depth of the ocean using sonar
find the distance of a submarine
why is ultrasound used in sonar

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the speed of sound in water by the time interval recorded.
Divide the total distance by 2 to find the one-way depth.

worked_examples.question_pattern: If there are {oscillations} density oscillations in {time} seconds at a given position, then calculate the frequency and time period.

solution_template.explain: Frequency is oscillations divided by time.
Time period is the inverse of frequency.

worked_examples.question_pattern: What is the wavelength in air for a frequency of {frequency} Hz if the speed of sound is {speed} m/s?

solution_template.explain: Wavelength is speed divided by frequency.

worked_examples.question_pattern: You clap in an empty corridor and hear an echo after {time} s. If the speed of sound in air is {speed} m/s, calculate your distance from the wall.
